release_notes: Table-UX release: the campaigns table's fixed identity columns become full peers of the metric columns, and every cell clips at its own boundary. Full column reorder — one unified persisted column order (orbitra_campaign_col_order) drives the header, the body rows, the totals row and the colgroup, so fixed columns (ID, Status, Campaign, Actions, Group) and metrics drag alike, header/body desync is structurally impossible, and a dragged order survives reloads; the old metric-only reorder that rewrote the customizer's visibility list is replaced. The fixed columns show their sort arrows again (they always sorted on click — the affordance was hidden since v1.3.2) and all five carry resize handles; Actions renders through the shared SortableTh with a new sortable=false prop (grip + resize, no arrow — nothing to sort by). Narrowed columns stop painting over their neighbours: overflow on td defaults to visible, so a narrowed column rendered its nowrap content straight over the neighbouring cell's text and icons while only the header clipped — every .tracker-table th/td now has overflow hidden + text-overflow ellipsis, rows paint an opaque background (hover still swaps the whole row), and buttons/icons inside flex cells keep their size (flex-shrink: 0) and get clipped rather than deformed. A long campaign name truncates to an ellipsis inside its cell (truncate is a no-op on inline boxes and the span was inline — it rendered onto the Group and Actions cells). Header labels centre within their column in every table (a label hugging the edge of a user-widened column reads crooked), and vertical middle alignment extends to .page-table (Domains, Networks, Sources, Trends, Conversions). Column reorder drags show a compact opaque chip naming the column instead of the browser's translucent snapshot of a whole wide header, and the drop target highlights with an opaque background + primary bar. The Actions column is sized for its four controls (150px, was 110 — the kebab landed on the Group column's text); the Namecheap toolbar buttons render disabled until the status resolves instead of popping in and reflowing the toolbar.
